property_summary: C.transfer always reverts when the _tos array is empty, regardless of other parameters.
When _tos is non-empty and the token call succeeds, C.transfer returns true after calling transferFrom once per destination.
For a non-empty destination list, C.transfer returns true when the underlying transferFrom calls succeed, making exactly one external call per destination.
For a single-element destination list, C.transfer returns true even when the token address has no code, since the low-level call to an empty address succeeds.
For a non-empty _tos and a token address with no code, C.transfer returns true even though no token transfer can actually occur (it accepts an empty success returndata as success).
If _tos.length > 0, transfer always returns true; if _tos is empty, transfer always reverts.

property_summary: For any non-empty _tos list, transfer always returns true and does not revert.
For an empty recipient list, C.transfer always reverts and makes no call; for any non-empty list, it returns true.
If the token address cannot handle transferFrom (here, C itself), C.transfer always reverts, even with a non-empty recipient list.
When the token address is a contract that accepts any call (this test contract's payable fallback), C.transfer returns true for a single-recipient list.
With a token whose transferFrom always succeeds, C.transfer reverts exactly when _tos is empty and otherwise returns true (performing one transferFrom per recipient).
